Colour
kŭl´er
n. (hue; appearance to the eye; Hebrew 'ayin, literally eye)
Latin color. The KJV keeps the older British spelling. The Hebrew word most often rendered colour is 'ayin, eye — the appearance of a thing to the eye rather than an abstract property of it.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Colour in Scripture is how a thing looks, and it is often diagnostic. The priest examining a plague in a garment is given colour as a test: “if the plague have not changed his colour, and the plague be not spread; it is unclean; thou shalt burn it in the fire” (Lev 13:55). The manna is described by it: “And the manna was as coriander seed, and the colour thereof as the colour of bdellium” (Num 11:7). Solomon uses it as a warning: “Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright” (Pro 23:31). And Ezekiel reaches for it twice in the first vision, where nothing quite fits: “out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire” (Eze 1:4), and of the living creatures, “they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass” (Eze 1:7). The Hebrew idiom is exact: what the eye of the beholder reports. Ezekiel does not say the wheels were amber. He says what they were like to look at, and stops there.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines colour as the appearance of bodies to the eye, or that property which is perceived by the organ of sight; also, appearance to the mind; pretence, false show.

expand to see more

COLOR, n. In physics, a property inherent in light, which by a difference in the rays and the laws of refraction produces different sensations.

2. Appearance of a body to the eye; hue; dye.

3. Appearance to the mind; false show; pretence; as, under color of law.

4. In the plural, a flag, ensign or standard.

Key Scripture

Lev 13:55 — "And the priest shall look on the plague, after that it is washed: and, behold, if the plague have not changed his colour, and the plague be not spread; it is unclean; thou shalt burn it in the fire; it is fret inward, whether it be bare within or without."

Pro 23:31 — "Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright."

Eze 1:4 — "And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire."

Eze 1:7 — "And their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot: and they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass."

Modern Corruption

Appearance is trusted as the measure of a thing, while Proverbs points at wine at its most beautiful and says do not look, and Ezekiel refuses to say more than what a thing resembled.

expand to see more

Proverbs 23:31 is one of the few places Scripture commands a man not to look at something beautiful. The verse describes the wine at its most attractive — red, catching the light, moving in the cup — and forbids the gaze rather than merely the drink, because the appetite is engaged by the eye before the mouth. The next verse names the end: at the last it biteth like a serpent. Temptation in Scripture is rarely ugly, and the counsel is rarely to look harder and reason better; it is to look away.

Ezekiel 1 shows the honest use of the word. Confronted with a vision of the glory, the prophet piles up comparisons — as the colour of amber, like the colour of burnished brass, the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD — and never once claims to describe the thing itself. That reticence is a doctrine. God is not less than what Ezekiel saw; He is more, and the prophet's hedged language is reverence, not vagueness.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'ayin (H5869), eye, and so appearance or colour; mar'eh (H4758), appearance, sight; tseva' (H6648), dyed stuff.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'ayin (H5869) — eye, appearance, colour; Numbers 11:7, Ezekiel 1:4.

Hebrew mar'eh (H4758) — appearance, vision; Ezekiel's repeated hedge.

Hebrew tsava' (H6648) — dyed garments, colours; Judges 5:30.

Hebrew chashmal (H2830) — amber; the colour out of the midst of the fire.

Hebrew nega' (H5061) — plague, stroke; the thing whose colour the priest examined.

Usage

"“If the plague have not changed his colour” — appearance as diagnosis."

"“Look not thou upon the wine… when it giveth his colour in the cup” — look away."

"“As the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire” — a likeness, not a description."
